Here is a detailed **7-Day China Trip Itinerary** following the classic "Golden Triangle" route — **Beijing → Xi'an → Chengdu** — perfect for first-time visitors!

---

# 🇨🇳 7-Day China Trip Itinerary: Beijing, Xi'an & Chengdu

For a well-balanced 7-day China itinerary, popular destinations such as Beijing, Xi'an, and Chengdu are highly recommended, as they offer iconic attractions and convenient transportation. These major cities have frequent high-speed trains and flights, giving you more flexibility and saving valuable travel time.

---

## 📅 Day 1 — Arrive in Beijing
- **Arrive at Beijing Capital International Airport.** Take the Airport Express train to the city center for ¥25 — it's a better option than taxis during rush hour.
- Spend the afternoon exploring **Tiananmen Square** and the surrounding area.
- Have dinner at a local Peking Duck restaurant to kick off your culinary adventure.

---

## 📅 Day 2 — Forbidden City & Temple of Heaven
- Visit Beijing's iconic royal landmarks, including the **Summer Palace**, **Temple of Heaven**, and the **Forbidden City**.
- The **Palace Museum** (Forbidden City) holds artifacts from ancient dynasties — the buildings cover over 180 acres and are a great place to learn about China's history.
- In the evening, explore the **Lama Temple** or the **798 Art District**. The 798 Art District is a platform of Chinese creativity and expression where artists display their works.

---

## 📅 Day 3 — The Great Wall
- Head out early to the **Great Wall of China**. Visit the **Mutianyu section** — it's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall.
- The Great Wall stretches over 21,000 kilometers and offers both busy tourist sections and secluded ruins.
- In the afternoon, fly or take the overnight train to **Xi'an**. Book a top bunk on the overnight train if you want more privacy at a lower price.

---

## 📅 Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Army
- Marvel at the world-renowned **Terracotta Army**, an extraordinary underground army guarding China's first emperor.
- Later, visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda**. An optional evening trip to **Great Tang All Day Mall** offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture.
- End the day at the **Muslim Quarter** food stalls. Try *Yang Rou Pao Mo* (bread soaked in lamb broth), but ask them to go light on the oil if you're not used to rich food.

---

## 📅 Day 5 — Xi'an City Wall → Chengdu
- Ride a bike along the ancient **Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. You can rent a bike for ¥45 to ride the full 14km wall circuit.
- Take the afternoon **bullet train to Chengdu**. Get to the station 90 minutes early for passport checks.
- End your day with **Sichuan hotpot** — but be ready for serious heat!

---

## 📅 Day 6 — Chengdu: Giant Pandas & Old Streets
- Get to the **Giant Panda Breeding Center** when it opens at 7:30 AM to see the pandas eat breakfast. Later, visit **People's Park** to watch locals play mahjong and practice tai chi. Finish your day in the **Kuanzhai Xiangzi alleys** where old meets new.
- After the panda experience, stroll down **Jinli Old Street** for souvenirs.

---

## 📅 Day 7 — Leshan Giant Buddha (Day Trip) & Departure
- **Leshan**, a 1.5-hour bullet train ride from Chengdu, is home to the world's largest carved stone Buddha. The sheer size of the Buddha is overwhelming, as he stretches more than 71 meters into the sky.
- Return to Chengdu and head to the airport for departure.

---

## 🧳 Essential Travel Tips

### 🛂 Visas
China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations — a 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance. If your country isn't on the 30-day visa-free list, the 240-hour (10-day) transit visa exemption is available to citizens of 55 countries at major ports of entry — seven days falls well within this window.

### 📱 Apps & Connectivity
- In China, some overseas websites are blocked — popular sites such as Google, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram are not accessible. It is strongly recommended that you purchase and install a **VPN** before arriving in China.
- Use **Amap** for navigation instead of Google Maps — it's in English, relatively user-friendly, and way more accurate. Apple Maps also works about 80% of the time.

### 💳 Payments
- Almost all vendors in China accept **mobile payments**, from large shopping malls to local vendors. The most popular options are **Alipay** and **WeChat Pay**.
- Although mobile payments are very common, credit cards and cash are still accepted. It's a good idea to bring your credit cards and exchange some cash for emergencies, especially for small vendors or local markets.

### 📆 Best Time to Visit
- **Spring (March to May)** is one of the best times to visit — temperatures are mild, flowers are in full bloom, and air quality tends to be better after winter.
- The best seasons are **April–May & September–October**. Avoid Golden Week (Oct 1–7) and Chinese New Year (Jan/Feb), as prices skyrocket and crowds are immense.

### 🪪 Passport
- Keep your passport with you at all times. You'll need it to enter attractions, ride high-speed trains, and check into hotels.

### 💰 Tipping
- Tipping isn't standard in China and is even considered offensive or rude in the culture. Whatever price you
